jobDescription: Our soft-drinks bottling plant is replacing two of its five filling lines over the next eighteen months. The Capital Projects Manager plans and controls these line replacement projects, manages the equipment suppliers and installation contractors, runs the site acceptance tests with production and quality, and reports cost and schedule to the plant capital board. The projects fall under the group's capital governance policy, which says that managers of projects above the approval threshold must be PMP certified; the certificate will be checked before an offer is made.
requirements: Plans and controls capital equipment projects with a baseline schedule and cost tracking.
Manages equipment suppliers and installation contractors, including contract change requests.
Runs site acceptance tests with production and quality teams.
Reports cost and schedule to a capital board or equivalent governance forum.
Holds the Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.

evidence.text: Project Engineer, Halden Dairy Products (March 2020 to September 2026): planned the replacement of a yoghurt cup filler and a case erector, keeping the baseline schedule in MS Project and tracking committed and actual cost against the approved budget.
Managed the filler supplier and two installation contractors during a three-week shutdown, logging each contract change request with its cost and the plant engineering manager's approval.
Wrote the site acceptance test protocol for the new filler with the production and quality leads and recorded each test result and deviation until the line was released back to production.
Prepared the monthly cost and schedule report for the site capital review, showing committed spend, forecast to complete and milestone status for each open project.
Maintenance Planner, Halden Dairy Products (August 2017 to February 2020): scheduled planned maintenance for the filling hall and kept the critical spares list for the fillers.

Work sample: the site acceptance test record for the yoghurt cup filler, with the test list, measured fill weights against specification, two deviations with their corrective actions and the signatures of the production and quality leads.
Recruiter screening note: on the phone the candidate said they 'got the PMP a couple of years ago' and offered to look for the certificate and send it after the interview.

Reference check summary: the plant engineering manager at Halden Dairy Products confirmed in writing that the candidate ran the cup filler replacement in 2023 and 2024 and wrote its site acceptance test protocol.

propositions.text: The candidate planned the replacement of a cup filler and a case erector with a baseline schedule and tracked committed and actual cost against the approved budget.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the schedule and cost tracking directly.

propositions.text: The candidate wrote the site acceptance test protocol for the new filler with the production and quality leads and recorded results and deviations.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the protocol work, the work sample is the signed test record and the plant engineering manager confirmed it in writing.

propositions.text: The candidate holds the Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
propositions.rationale: The certification appears only as the candidate's own remark on a screening call, with no certificate, number, date or register check; the qualification rule forbids calling a candidate certified without explicit cited evidence.

gold.expectedGap: The PMP certification is not established; it rests on the candidate's remark during screening, with no certificate number, award date or register record.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the documented planning, supplier, acceptance-test and capital reporting work and the confirmed filler project; do not describe the candidate as PMP certified.
followUpTargets: Ask for the PMP certification number and award date so the certification can be checked on PMI's online certification registry.
